dr_grpo_nostd_limit.claim: With scale_rewards='none' (Dr-GRPO), E[sum_i (r_i - mean r) grad log pi(y_i)] = (G-1) p grad log pi(gold) = (G-1) grad p, for every G. The limit is CE weighted by p (normalised to 2p at p=0.5), independent of G; it upweights EASY images, the opposite of the std version
dr_grpo_nostd_limit.check: exact enumeration equals (G-1)p for G in {4,8,16}, p in {0.1,0.5,0.9} (assert, 1e-12); Monte Carlo 200k draws: G8 p0.3 2.1003 vs 2.1, G4 p0.7 2.1001 vs 2.1 (next/calc.py, python3 -I)
dr_grpo_nostd_limit.consequence: This corrects the base design, which called the Dr-GRPO limit 'w8(p)/w8(0.5)'. With screening at band B_G, the screened Dr-GRPO limit is CE x 2p x 1[p in B_G]. Larger G only lowers variance and widens B_G
dr_grpo_nostd_limit.ignored: KL (beta=0 here), token-length normalisation, the max_grad_norm=1.0 clip (binds on every useful RL400 step, runs/aircraft-controlled400-diagnosis-v1/report.md)
dr_grpo_nostd_limit.clip_caveat: Amendment 1 (design review finding 2). The limit is of the UNCLIPPED expected gradient. With one prompt per update RL's expected step is E[clip(g_hat)], not clip(E[g_hat]), and a supervised arm's step is clip(w x g_CE). Measured: CE pre-clip grad_norm > 1.0 on 47.3% (sft-1e5, 2,464 steps), 34.4% (sft-5e5, 2,864) and 32.6% (sft-1e4, 2,824) of controlled400 SFT steps, and on 137/400 = 34.3% of RL400 steps (all of its mixed steps); instrument: python3 -I over runs/aircraft-controlled400-v1/work/*/trainer_state.json log_history grad_norm (pre-clip; optimizer_audit.jsonl latest_gradient_norm is POST-clip, max 1.0000000107 on RL400). So on roughly a third to a half of CE steps the clip rescales the step to norm 1 and A2's 2p factor is erased there (A2 is then band-masked CE on those steps); the clip is kept (fixed profile, identical for RL and every supervised arm and for the whole strongest-SFT pool lineage), and the Gate A claim is narrowed accordingly (gates GA fail_claim).

algebra.hn_reward_limit: Corrected by amendment 1 (design review finding 3). For any reward, the Dr-GRPO expected update is (G-1) grad E_pi[r]. For exact_hn (r(gold)=1, r(c)=-0.5 for every frozen-map confuser c of the gold) that is (G-1)[p grad log pi(gold) - 0.5 sum_{c in M(gold)} pi(c) grad log pi(c)], times the screen band: a p-weighted gold term and an unweighted sum over ALL map confusers. A3 (unweighted CE + 0.5 grad[-log(1 - pi(c))] = 0.5 pi(c)/(1 - pi(c)) grad log pi(c) on the single top live confuser, no band) is NOT this limit, and the draft's 'gold gradient plus 0.5 x unlikelihood pressure on c (up to the same group weighting)' was wrong. Resolution: exact_hn is not used by this study; A3 is a supervised comparator (Stage A arms, gates GA), never coupled to an RL reward or to LIM-T.

hypotheses.HA: Amended (amendment 1). The supervised limit of screened exact-reward Dr-GRPO (A2: CE x stopgrad[2p] x 1[p in B_8], no optimizer step outside the band) beats the best of plain CE (A1), HN-SFT (A3) and constrained CE (A5) on H-select by >= +0.03 sampled macro, with a Bonferroni-adjusted (3 candidates) small-n-corrected paired LB > 0, under the fixed profile (max_grad_norm 1.0, one prompt per update, constant AdamW)
hypotheses.HB: Only if HA: screened Dr-GRPO (beta=0, exact reward) from I* beats the strongest fair SFT on native VAL by the unchanged substantial_rl margins
hypotheses.HB_robust: The HB gain also survives the limit objective (A2's) continued from I* to equal active time (LIM-T), at seed 42 and in every replicate seed's pool
hypotheses.decision_rule_note: Amendment 1 (design review minor finding 10). If RL behaves like its own limit it cannot beat LIM-T (about 13x more updates at G8) by +0.05, so passing Gate A raises the bar for Stage B rather than predicting its success: Stage B can pass only if the clipped, finite-G, single-sample RL update does something its expected-gradient limit does not. That is the hypothesis HB tests; a Gate A pass is necessary for spending on it, not evidence for it

design_review_v1.source: PR #26 design review (aircraft-signal-limit-v1), 5 blocking + 10 minor; the reviewer edited nothing and ran nothing. Verdicts below were checked against the repository; where a verdict rests on a measurement, the instrument is named
design_review_v1.confirmed_sound_by_reviewer: Dr-GRPO (G-1)p claim (re-derived by hand; the gold term includes the ~3% non-canonical tokenisations, which egsft's p already sums), no VAL/TEST in RL selection, max-VAL strongest SFT, C* as a maximum, a_floor and its 375/987 boundary, compute-plan sums, D_req 0.05

findings.finding: n = 2 images per class on H-select and H-gate: the within-class bootstrap has (n-1)/n = 0.5 of the variance, so Gate A and G3 bounds pass too easily
findings.check: 2 images x 100 classes in both manifests (python3 -I Counter over runs/aircraft-freshpool-g0-v1/manifests/h_select.jsonl, h_gate.jsonl); the plug-in variance algebra is standard
findings.resolution: bootstrap.small_n_correction, applied to Gate A (ii) and G3a in the evaluator; forced fire in tests (a plain LB of +0.02 becomes -0.013)

findings.finding: max_grad_norm 1.0 clip undoes the RL ~ limit premise; Gate A's verdict says nothing about RL
findings.check: pre-clip grad_norm > 1 on 32.6-47.3% of controlled400 CE steps and 34.3% of RL400 steps (algebra clip_caveat instrument), i.e. the clip binds often but not on most CE steps
findings.resolution: Gate A's negative and positive claims narrowed (gates GA fail_claim / pass_claim), clip fraction per arm and among A2's in-band steps reported. Rejected part: removing the clip in Stage A/B, because the clip is part of the fixed profile shared by RL, every supervised arm and the whole strongest-SFT pool lineage (controlled400, W, I), and dropping it would need its own LR grid and break comparability with the pool; no Stage 0 measurement is added because the pre-clip norm is already logged on every step of every arm (trainer_state.json grad_norm)

findings.finding: A3 is not the limit of exact_hn, so the A3 branch of Stage B (RL reward and LIM-T) is uninterpretable
findings.check: re-derived: Dr-GRPO E[update] = (G-1) grad E[r] for any reward (algebra.hn_reward_limit)
findings.resolution: the A3 -> exact_hn coupling is dropped: A2 is the only Gate A candidate (Bonferroni over 3), A3 is a supervised comparator in C* and the protocol pool and stays an I* candidate, RL always uses the exact reward, LIM-T always continues A2. Defining A3 as the exact limit was rejected: it needs a teacher-forced pass with gradient for every map confuser of every image (up to 10, for A320; mean 1.58 over the 100 labels, python3 -I over data/fgvc-aircraft-2013b/audit/p0-confusion-map.json) and a new trainer mode: a modest compute cost but a new, model-untested loss surface added after review, for a reward whose signal the forensics put in a minority of groups (29/128 hold a valid wrong answer, parent_failure_facts.format_only_mixed_groups)

findings.finding: A2's out-of-band images count as updates and take phantom AdamW momentum steps; A2 mixes p-weighting, data reduction and momentum noise
findings.check: constant AdamW with a zero gradient still steps by lr x m_hat / (sqrt(v_hat) + eps); test_egsft_band_skips_the_optimizer_step_and_leaves_adamw_state_untouched
findings.resolution: out-of-band images take no optimizer step (parameters, moments and step count untouched), the presentation still counts, so A2 stays data-matched to every arm on the same 600 S_a images; its in-band step count is reported and Gate A's claim is narrowed to the data-matched limit. Matching informative updates instead was rejected: at W's predicted G8 acceptance 0.42, 600 in-band steps need ~1,430 presentations, more than S_a's 1,040 images, so A2 would see more labelled images or repeats than A1/A3/A5 and confound data with objective

findings.finding: the claim rests on the robust verdict, but G5, G3b and G6 do not use the robust pool
findings.resolution: G3b gates on RL* - LIM-T >= +0.05; G5's per-seed pool is the robust one (seed-independent robust members plus the seed's SFT-E, SFT-T and its own LIM-T, run per replicate seed); G6 names the robust-verdict strongest SFT (what the evaluator already did)

findings.finding: Gate A tests A2 at B_8 though GB0 may choose G16; token-mean CE vs dr_grpo sequence-sum differ by 1/len(gold)
findings.resolution: gates GA band_note; LIM-T already uses the chosen G's band. Rerunning Stage A at B_16 after GB0 would put a Stage A arm after a Stage B look, and changing A2 to a sequence sum would change the EG-SFT objective the lineage measured

findings.finding: G2's invalid <= I* + 2 fires under the null
findings.resolution: slack max(2, 2 sqrt(a + b)), two Poisson SDs of the difference

findings.finding: cost caps rest on one probe step; c(G16) extrapolated; E0 only at G8
findings.resolution: Stage 0 measures c(G8) and c(G16) over >= 8 accepted steps each and proves E0 at both; the launcher refuses a Stage 0 fragment without e0_groups [8, 16] and c_accepted_steps >= 8 per G; +1.6 h estimate

findings.finding: PI can stop the whole study on a proxy init, blocking Stage A's clean negative; PI ignores sampled validity
findings.resolution: PI is advisory: it publishes forecast checks, including sampled validity >= 0.95, and never stops; GB0 at I* stays binding

findings.finding: SFT-T has no checkpoint selection; overtraining makes G3b easier
findings.resolution: stages Stage B SFT-T checkpoints note: SFT-E(lr) is SFT-T's start and is already gated in G3a and pooled at VAL, mirroring RL's 100/300 two-point selection; an intermediate checkpoint grid was rejected because every extra checkpoint is another H-select assay (~0.5 h each) and another VAL endpoint, and the robust verdict, not G3b, carries the claim

findings.resolution: .md section 4 now says +1.2 pp (sft-1e5-time, the strongest) and +1.7 pp for sft-5e5-time

G4 says 'vs init W' but Stage B starts from I*
findings.resolution: G4 pass text states the protocol's init is W and I* sits in both pools

Native VAL (G4, G5) and sealed TEST (G6) only through the native-VAL package, never by this launch.

execution.executor: UWaterloo Engineering hosts through ~/.claude/bin/uwrun; this Mac only sequences, gates and journals (plan execution: uwaterloo)
execution.replaces: fixed_profile.model's 'FP32 MPS' device. The protocol's activation prerequisites name 'the chosen device'; this is it: CPU FP32 on AMD Ryzen 9 5900X hosts (ecetesla1/2/4, one hardware class), 16 torch threads per stage. dtype stays FP32.
execution.why_not_gpu: The RTX 2080 Ti (the only FP32-capable GPU, 11 GiB) ran SFT and GRPO G8 but GRPO G16 FP32 ran out of memory, and Stage 0 must prove E0 and measure c(G) at G16 (GB0 may choose it); G8 peaked at 10.0 of 10.6 GiB beside another user's process. The RTX 3070s (8 GiB) cannot hold the 8.8 GB FP32 weights. Receipts: cost_receipts.
execution.one_device_class: Every stage of the study (P0-I, Stage 0, Stage A, P0', RL, SFT-E, SFT-T, LIM-T, every H assay) runs on this one device class, so budget matching in active seconds (T_RL, caps) and every H comparison is within one device.
disclosed: W, I and the six controlled400 SFT pool endpoints were trained on MPS FP32; their native-VAL scores (a*) were measured on MPS. CPU FP32 numerics differ from MPS FP32 at the ULP level (kernel order); a new endpoint's VAL runs on the native-VAL package's own device.

Shared hosts: other users' work runs beside a stage. The host probe requires the stage's 16 threads idle (nproc - load1) when it starts; wall-time caps include any later contention (an arm that hits its 1.25x cap stops the study, pre-registered).
